question: Milkha Singh, the Flying Sikh, was the first Indian to win a gold medal in which of the following games?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Commonwealth Games.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh**, also known as the **Flying Sikh**, won a **gold medal** in the **400m race** at the **Commonwealth Games** held in **Cardiff in 1958.**
 
• In the Asian Games in **1958 and 1962,** he also took home gold medals. 
 
• For his athletic accomplishments, he was given the** Padma Shri, **the fourth-highest civilian honor in India.
 
• Singh was referred to as "**the finest athlete India has ever produced"** by columnist Rohit Brijnath in** 2008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardiff, Wales **hosted the **1958 British Empire** and **Commonwealth Games** from **July 18–26.**
 
• A total of 1,130 competitors and 228 officials were sent by **35 nations** to the Cardiff Games.
 
• The **Queen's Baton Relay** was also inaugurated during the 1958 event.
 
• On the first leg of the Queen's Baton's voyage to Wales, two of England's most renowned middle distance runners,** Roger Bannister and Chris Chattaway,** were given the honor of accepting it at **Buckingham Palace.**
